# Draft Commerce Component Spec

Produces new draft spec(s) for `examples/kit-nextjs-commerce-starter`, consistent with the existing baseline docs and specs under `examples/kit-nextjs-commerce-starter/commerce-specs/`.

## When to Use

- Drafting a spec for a **new** commerce component (Sitecore-registered rendering) that doesn't exist yet.
- The new component needs a **helper** (non-registered, consumed-by-another-component) piece too — e.g. a new container needs a presentational card, or a new leaf component needs a data-fetching helper like `OrderCloudProductList`.
- Researching an OrderCloud model or service to ground a spec in real field names/operations before writing it.
- **Executing** an already-drafted spec: implementing it as real code in `examples/kit-nextjs-commerce-starter`.
- **Promoting** a draft the user has finished testing, out of `drafts/` into `component-specs/`.

Not for editing/reorganizing the already-finalized specs in `commerce-specs/component-specs/` (outside `drafts/`) — only move things there via the promotion flow below, once the user has tested an executed draft.

## Inputs to Gather (ask only what's missing)

- Component name (PascalCase) and a one-line purpose.
- Sitecore-registered rendering (server or client, variant names) vs. a pure helper.
- Does it need to live inside a `ProductContainer` (consumes `ProductDataContext`) or is it standalone/self-sourcing (like `ProductListing`)?
- Which OrderCloud model(s)/service(s) it touches.

## Procedure

1. **Read the baseline docs, every time, in this order:**
   - [commerce-component-patterns.md](../../../examples/kit-nextjs-commerce-starter/commerce-specs/commerce-component-patterns.md) — §1 container+context, §2 product/list-source resolution, §3 XP data/presentation split, §4 established best practices, §5 known gaps.
   - [common-component-patterns.md](../../../examples/kit-nextjs-commerce-starter/commerce-specs/common-component-patterns.md) — defensive datasource access, editor/authoring-safe state ladder. Do not edit this file; only follow it.
   - [component-specs/index.md](../../../examples/kit-nextjs-commerce-starter/commerce-specs/component-specs/index.md) — the component inventory (what exists, where, and its spec).
   - [templates-and-renderings.md](../../../examples/kit-nextjs-commerce-starter/commerce-specs/templates-and-renderings.md) — confirmed field/template schemas, so new field names don't collide with what's already authored in the live environment. It's populated only via Sitecore CLI serialization pulls from the live environment; treat it as read-only reference and never write to it from this skill.
   - The 1-2 existing specs closest in shape to what's being drafted, e.g. [product-container.md](../../../examples/kit-nextjs-commerce-starter/commerce-specs/component-specs/product-container.md) for a container-style component, [product-listing.md](../../../examples/kit-nextjs-commerce-starter/commerce-specs/component-specs/product-listing.md) for a standalone/source-resolving component, or [spec-form.md](../../../examples/kit-nextjs-commerce-starter/commerce-specs/component-specs/spec-form.md) + [helpers/product-spec-fields.md](../../../examples/kit-nextjs-commerce-starter/commerce-specs/component-specs/helpers/product-spec-fields.md) for a component+helper pair.

2. **Research the OrderCloud side.** For each OrderCloud model/service the component touches, check both:
   - The types already used in `src/lib/commerce/**` of the starter (e.g. `ordercloud-javascript-sdk` types like `BuyerProduct`, `Spec`, `LineItem`, `Order`, `Category`) — these are ground truth for what this codebase actually sends/receives.
   - The official OrderCloud API reference at `https://ordercloud.io/api-reference` (fetch the specific resource page, e.g. Products, Specs, Orders, LineItems, Categories, Promotions, Buyers) to confirm field names, required/optional-ness, and available operations beyond what's already used in this codebase.
   - Call out any mismatch between the two explicitly in the draft rather than silently picking one.

3. **Decide file placement** (paths from repo root). The archive layout and promote rules are in [commerce-specs/README.md](../../../examples/kit-nextjs-commerce-starter/commerce-specs/README.md).
   - New Sitecore-registered component → `examples/kit-nextjs-commerce-starter/commerce-specs/component-specs/drafts/<kebab-case-name>.md`.
   - New non-registered helper → `examples/kit-nextjs-commerce-starter/commerce-specs/component-specs/helpers/drafts/<kebab-case-name>.md`.
   - Component + helper together → create both, cross-linked the same way `spec-form.md` links to `helpers/product-spec-fields.md`.
   - **Cross-cutting slice** (one unit of work that updates several existing surfaces, not a single new rendering) → still one file in `component-specs/drafts/<kebab-case-name>.md`. Do not create sibling folders such as `slices/` or `wip/`. On promote, fold the draft into the affected promoted specs and delete the draft (or split out a new helper file if one shipped).
   - Create the `drafts/` directory if it doesn't exist yet.

4. **Write the draft** using [the template](./references/template.md) — match the structure and tone of existing specs (frontmatter, `> Part of ...` breadcrumb, Summary, Sitecore template/rendering, Manual Content Editor Instructions, Props/datasource shape, Behavior, Known gaps).
   - Mark any Sitecore template/rendering fields as **proposed** (not confirmed) unless you've verified them via a live serialization pull — don't present invented field data as confirmed the way [templates-and-renderings.md](../../../examples/kit-nextjs-commerce-starter/commerce-specs/templates-and-renderings.md) does for existing components.
   - **For every Sitecore-registered component**, include a "Manual Content Editor Instructions" section: concrete, numbered steps for what a human with CM access must create in the live environment (datasource template, rendering item + its datasource template/location, any Placeholder Settings entries, any droplist/lookup source items, Standard Values defaults) before the component can be authored/tested. If the component is a pure leaf rendering with no datasource template (like `AddToCart`/`SpecForm`/`ProductInfo`), say so explicitly rather than omitting the section. Helpers don't get this section — they aren't independently registered in Sitecore.
   - Reuse the container+context pattern and the three-way source model (CMS-authored / live catalog / manually picked) rather than inventing new state-management or sourcing approaches; if a genuine deviation is needed, say so explicitly and why.
   - Include a "Known gaps / open questions" section, same as existing specs.

5. **Update navigation:** add a row for the new draft to the relevant table in [component-specs/index.md](../../../examples/kit-nextjs-commerce-starter/commerce-specs/component-specs/index.md), labeled `(draft)`.

6. **Never** write to `templates-and-renderings.md` — it only reflects what's been pulled via Sitecore CLI serialization from the live environment. A drafted, executed, or even promoted spec doesn't get an entry there until it's actually confirmed against a real CM pull.

## Executing a Draft

Do this when the user asks to implement, build, or execute an existing drafted spec (component draft, and its paired helper draft if any) into real code.

1. Read the full draft spec file(s) end to end, including the Manual Content Editor Instructions section (you won't perform it, but it tells you what won't exist in Sitecore yet).
2. Implement the component(s) under `examples/kit-nextjs-commerce-starter/src/`, following this repo's established conventions (root `CLAUDE.md`/`Agents.md`, plus `commerce-component-patterns.md` and `common-component-patterns.md`):
   - Registered component → `src/components/<kebab-case-name>/<ComponentName>.tsx` (+ `<kebab-case-name>.props.ts` if it reads Sitecore fields directly), registered in `.sitecore/component-map.ts` (server) or the client component map, under the exact name used in the spec.
   - Helper → `src/components/commerce/<ComponentName>.tsx`, not registered anywhere.
   - Reuse existing contexts/services (`ProductDataContext`, `OrderCloudContext`, `RoutePathContext`, `lib/commerce/**`) instead of re-implementing equivalents — check for an existing helper/util first.
   - Implement the Behavior section as written (container+context pattern, defensive datasource access, editor/authoring-safe state ladder). If reality in the code diverges from what the draft describes, update the draft spec to match rather than leaving it stale.
3. Validate: run `npm install` (if needed), then `npm run build` and `npm run lint` from `examples/kit-nextjs-commerce-starter/`. Fix errors before reporting back.
4. Do **not** perform the Manual Content Editor Instructions yourself, move the file out of `drafts/`, change its `status`, or touch `component-specs/index.md` — implementation alone doesn't promote a draft.
5. Once it builds clean, tell the user: what was implemented and where, that they still need to complete the draft's **Manual Content Editor Instructions** by hand in the live Sitecore environment, and to test the component (authoring/preview and live) — then either confirm it works or come back with changes.

## Promoting a Tested Draft

Only after the user explicitly confirms they've finished testing an executed draft, ask whether they're ready to promote it out of `drafts/`. If they report issues instead, go back to step 2 of Executing a Draft (or back to drafting) — don't promote.

If they confirm yes:

1. Move the file: `drafts/<name>.md` → the parent folder (`component-specs/<name>.md`, or `component-specs/helpers/<name>.md` for a helper). If the draft was a **cross-cutting slice**, do not leave a sibling `slices/` file: fold the content into the promoted specs it changed, add any new helper files, then delete the draft.
2. Fix the file's own relative links now that it's one directory shallower — e.g. a component draft's `[../index.md]` becomes `[index.md]`; a helper draft's `[../../index.md]` becomes `[../index.md]`, and `[../<component>.md]` becomes `[<component>.md]`. Re-check every link in the file, don't assume only the breadcrumb line needs it.
3. Update the frontmatter `status` field to reflect the new state (e.g. `reviewed`, `implemented`) — ask the user what value their project uses if unclear; don't invent a status vocabulary.
4. Update its row in [component-specs/index.md](../../../examples/kit-nextjs-commerce-starter/commerce-specs/component-specs/index.md): drop the `(draft)` label, keep the link pointing at the new path. For a cross-cutting slice, remove the draft row and point inventory rows at the promoted specs you folded into.
5. Still never touch `templates-and-renderings.md` at any point in this workflow — it's only updated via a live CM serialization pull, never hand-edited as part of drafting/executing/promoting a spec.

## Output

Report back: which file(s) were created and where, which patterns from `commerce-component-patterns.md` were reused (or deviated from, and why), which OrderCloud docs/SDK types were consulted, and any open questions/gaps flagged in the draft.
